stories.title: Seoul's new buildings will supply 8 per cent of its electricity
stories.summary: Buildings approved in Seoul between 2022 and 2026 are expected to generate 3,811 gigawatt hours of renewable energy a year, thanks to city rules requiring solar facades and geothermal heating. That is 1.5 times the annual capacity of the Seoul Thermal Power Plant. The power station has been outdesigned.

stories.title: A LEED Platinum factory in Bangladesh stays 4.33 degrees cooler
stories.summary: A LEED Platinum garment factory in Rangpur, run by Karupannya Rangpur Ltd., kept indoor air an average of 4.33 degrees Celsius cooler than outdoors in the warm season, a case study in City and Built Environment found. A nearby conventional building managed only 1.67 degrees.

stories.title: Australian architects say renovate before you rebuild for net zero
stories.summary: The Australian Institute of Architects released its Zero Carbon Housing Challenge findings on Saturday, analysing the environmental impact of more than 330 homes. Net zero homes are already being built in Australia, it says, and more could cut their footprint through smarter design, better materials and renovation.

stories.title: Qatar's 3D printed school nears completion
stories.summary: UCC Holding says its school in Qatar, with 30,000 square metres of 3D printed walls, is taking final shape as the roof, windows, doors and interior finishes go in. Printing began in June 2025 with a COBOD printer. It is billed as the largest 3D printed building ever constructed.

stories.title: USGBC launches version two of its TRUE zero waste certification
stories.summary: The US Green Building Council has launched TRUE v2, the latest version of its zero waste certification programme. The council says the new version emphasises zero waste impacts and global applicability, and helps organisations with decarbonisation, business transformation and circularity goals. TRUE launched a decade ago.

stories.title: Studio Bua plans a breathable hempcrete home in Suffolk
stories.summary: Studio Bua is designing a hempcrete home in Suffolk for clients who live in a listed cob and thatch cottage and want the same comfort. The cottage's deep reveals and thermal mass keep it cool in summer and warm in winter. The practice has consulted Modece Architects on hemp lime.

stories.title: Radisson says a South African safari hotel is Africa's first Verified Net Zero hotel
stories.summary: Radisson Hotel Group says Radisson Safari Hotel Hoedspruit is Africa's first Verified Net Zero hotel, after changes to energy, dining, waste, water and procurement. Its programme runs hotels on 100 per cent renewable energy and covers residual emissions with carbon removal credits. Net zero, with an asterisk for removals.

stories.title: Diamond Schmitt to talk mass timber at a Canadian research centre
stories.summary: Diamond Schmitt's Sarah Low will present the Atlantic Science Enterprise Centre at the 2026 Wood Solutions Conference in Moncton on 18 November. The centre is a new federal research facility and regional headquarters that will bring five government departments together under one mass timber roof.

stories.title: Ahmedabad's Sardar Patel Bhavan passes a quake check but needs monitoring
stories.summary: An assessment of Sardar Patel Bhavan in Ahmedabad finds the historic municipal building compatible with the city's seismic zone. It is also showing minor subsidence and several visible signs of deterioration. Safety, Urban Acres notes, depends on continued monitoring and maintenance. The building has not been told it passed.

stories.title: India Biennale to spread art and architecture across Delhi's monuments
stories.summary: The second India Biennale opens in Delhi on 4 December, covering contemporary art, architecture, design and cultural exchange across historic monuments, museums, galleries and public spaces, PTI reports. The Ministry of Culture event is touted as the centre of a flagship celebration of contemporary art.

stories.title: An archive of Satish Gujral, who designed buildings without training as an architect
stories.summary: An Architectural Digest India essay revisits archival images of Satish Gujral, whose murals filled major public buildings in Delhi. Gujral did not train as an architect. The writer says he brought a sculptor's hand that shaped material into volumes and voids.

stories.title: An Uttarakhand home for four generations keeps the verandah and courtyard
stories.summary: Sukoon, a multigenerational home in Uttarakhand designed by Garima Agarwal of MN Design Co., gathers craft, art and textiles from several states. The brief asked for a house rooted in Indian classicism for four generations of educationists. Verandah and courtyard return as living spaces, still bringing in light and ventilation.

stories.title: Revisiting the Bihar Museum, a campus of pavilions and courtyards
stories.summary: STIRworld revisits the Bihar Museum in Patna, designed by Maki and Associates with Mumbai practice Opolis after a competition. Instead of one iconic structure, it is a series of buildings arranged as a campus around pavilions and courtyards. The piece first ran in the mondo arc india journal.

stories.title: Uttar Pradesh plans a Singapore City near Noida airport
stories.summary: The Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority said on 30 October that Uttar Pradesh will develop a Singapore City in Sector 7 near Noida International Airport at Jewar. The area, aimed at high end customers, will get investment from Singapore, officials said. Singapore itself took a little longer.

stories.title: Architects on designing for feeling, not just form
stories.summary: Forbes India's M-Connect series brought together Carl Bhesania of Talati and Partners and other architects to discuss how light, temperature, sound, proportion and material shape how a building feels. The episode was powered by Marmo Solutions. Calm and belonging, it turns out, also come in marble.

stories.title: Pittsburgh's Mill 19 turns a steel mill into a robotics hub
stories.summary: Mill 19, once part of the Jones and Laughlin steel mill in Pittsburgh, has been repurposed into a hub for tech, robotics and advanced manufacturing, The Guardian reports. When the steel industry collapsed in the 1970s and 1980s, it left a hole that needed to be filled, says John Buechli.

stories.title: Foster and MANICA unveil a 71,500 seat stadium for Milan's two clubs
stories.summary: Foster + Partners and MANICA have unveiled Generali Stadium, a 71,500 seat arena that will be the shared home of AC Milan and Inter. Stands of 11,700 fans rise behind each goal under a roof engineered to channel their roar back to the pitch. Its stonework references Milan's Duomo.

stories.title: KPF's Waterline becomes the tallest building in Texas
stories.summary: KPF has completed Waterline, a 1,025 foot, 74 storey mixed use tower on Lady Bird Lake in Austin, now the tallest building in Texas. It combines a hotel, offices, retail and luxury residences, and slopes away from the water as it rises. Houston held the record for a long time.

stories.title: Gluck+ stacks a film studio campus onto one New York block
stories.summary: Gluck+ designed Sunnyside Studios, a 350,000 square foot soundstage complex in New York. Studio campuses are usually spread out as backlots linked by golf carts. This one compresses stages, support, loading, parking, catering, crew and talent onto a single urban block. The golf carts were not consulted.

stories.title: A 1958 Prouvé house moves across France and becomes a holiday rental
stories.summary: Maison Prouvé 58, a prefabricated house by Jean Prouvé and his son Claude, was saved from demolition in Epfig, Alsace, dismantled, restored and rebuilt near Saint-Paul-de-Vence. The L-shaped house now sits among pine and olive trees and takes overnight guests through Les Maisons CAB.

stories.title: Em-Estudio lines a Mexico City basement bar with books
stories.summary: Em-Estudio designed Libreria Valladolid, a basement bar beneath an early 20th century house in Mexico City's Roma neighbourhood, to evoke the area's vintage bookstores. The studio says it captures the thrill of searching old bookshops for a story that has been waiting. Drinks and reading, in that order.

stories.title: A quiet timber garden studio for a London filmmaker and artist
stories.summary: O'Sullivan Skoufoglou Architects built a pared back garden studio in Highbury for a filmmaker and an artist. A low brick base anchors the timber structure, set in the leafy garden of a Victorian home, giving a calm, well lit workspace with strong views of the outdoors.

stories.title: Hale Brown restores Holborn's Sicilian Avenue
stories.summary: Hale Brown Architects has completed the preservation and modernisation of Sicilian Avenue in Holborn, one of London's earliest pedestrianised streets. The Grade II listed avenue was designed by R J Worley in 1910 for the Bedford Estate as shops and homes, with some housing later turned into offices.

stories.title: Meinhard von Gerkan's Latvian villa with a treetop tower is for sale
stories.summary: Villa Guna in Jurmala, Latvia, designed by Meinhard von Gerkan of GMP and built in the 2000s, is for sale by its original owner. The 635 square metre house has a U-shaped plan facing the Baltic forest and a 15 metre observation tower that rises through the pines.

stories.title: Ole Scheeren designs a digital art gallery folded into a Daegu landscape
stories.summary: Buro Ole Scheeren has unveiled Suseong Continuum, a digital media art gallery in Daegu, South Korea, commissioned for the Suseong International Biennale. The project sits in the site's existing topography and links exhibition spaces, outdoor paths and public areas into one continuous route between nature and screens.

stories.title: A Sao Paulo apartment built around a checkerboard floor
stories.summary: Kuster Brizola Arquitetos designed a 200 square metre apartment in Brooklin, Sao Paulo, for a couple with two children, making a checkerboard floor the main protagonist. The pattern organises the social area for a family that wanted a home for hosting friends and relatives. The chess set is presumably elsewhere.

stories.title: An equestrian complex outside Guadalajara for horses and quiet
stories.summary: Mendiola Arregui designed Rancho del Abuelo, a 994 square metre equestrian complex in Jalisco on the outskirts of Guadalajara. The programme pairs spaces for sheltering and caring for horses with others for resting, gathering and contemplation. The horses get the stables, the people get the contemplation.

stories.title: Dezeen's most popular houses of October
stories.summary: Dezeen's monthly roundup of its most popular houses for October includes an architect's pink postmodern dreamhouse and a home for children that looks like a wooden wardrobe. Other picks range from a bungalow conversion in northern England to luxury villas in Ibiza and Switzerland.

stories.title: Assam opens a plant that turns Brahmaputra silt into AAC blocks
stories.summary: Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma inaugurated a Rs 55 crore green AAC block plant in Tinsukia on Thursday, set up by Litebricks Pvt. Ltd. It uses Brahmaputra sediment as raw material, aiming to cut reliance on red bricks, protect farmland and create jobs in Upper Assam.

stories.title: Meta signs on for certificates tied to Fortera's low carbon cement
stories.summary: Low carbon cement maker Fortera has signed a multi-year deal to supply Meta with environmental attribute certificates linked to about 200,000 tonnes of its cement. Meta keeps the option to use the cement in its own buildings. For now it has bought the paperwork.

stories.title: Hasslacher closes an Austrian glulam plant as construction slumps
stories.summary: Austrian mass timber group Hasslacher will close its Gemson glulam plant in Rangersdorf and move production to three other Austrian sites by year end. It blamed a four year decline in building construction. Most of the 40 workers will stay with the group, and the hall's future is undecided.

stories.title: Thailand adds BIM and green construction skills to national training
stories.summary: Thailand is folding digital and environmentally focused construction skills, including BIM, into its national skills and vocational training frameworks, with backing from the International Labour Organization. The ILO said the move came from cooperation between government, employers, workers and the construction industry.

stories.title: Rajasthan has over 750 IGBC green building projects
stories.summary: Rajasthan has registered more than 750 green building projects with the Indian Green Building Council, spanning over 23 crore square feet, industry representatives said at the Green Rajasthan Conference in Jaipur. CII-IGBC chairman C Shekhar Reddy urged extending the practice to industrial parks, townships and public infrastructure.

stories.title: Jewar airport's terminal draws on Varanasi's ghats and jaali screens
stories.summary: Outlook Luxe looks past the renaming of Noida International Airport to its terminal at Jewar, designed by a consortium of Grimshaw, Nordic Office of Architecture, Haptic and STUP after a three stage competition in 2020. The design draws on Varanasi's ghats and intricate jaali screens.

stories.title: A terracotta jaali and a rain tree shade a Bengaluru showroom
stories.summary: AD Studio 9 turned 6,000 square feet of commercial space in Bengaluru into the Kara Veneer showroom, keeping a mature rain tree outside its western wall. A terracotta lattice facade cuts solar heat gain from the afternoon sun. The tree was treated as part of the project, not an obstacle.

stories.title: The Northeast's stilt houses still carry ancestral climate wisdom
stories.summary: The New Indian Express looks at the stilted houses of the Northeast, raised on bamboo, timber or stone poles above the uneven ground of Assam, Nagaland and Meghalaya. They are built from locally available materials and reflect the occupations of the people who live in them.

stories.title: Laurie Baker's Costford cleared to build Karimadom Colony flats
stories.summary: Thiruvananthapuram's district planning committee approved the long stalled rehabilitation project for 128 families in Karimadom Colony. The corporation plans to release 20 per cent of the cost to Costford, Laurie Baker's institute, which will build four blocks of 32 flats each. The corporation first launched the project in 2008.

stories.title: Himachal villages already use 25 community climate adaptation measures
stories.summary: A CEEW study supported by ICIMOD documented 25 community led adaptation solutions across Mandi, Kullu, Shimla and Sirmaur. They range from new crop patterns and natural farming to reviving traditional water sources and village disaster preparedness. Findings were shared at a dialogue in Shimla on Saturday.

stories.title: An essay asks who Bengaluru is being built for
stories.summary: An ArchitectureLive essay contrasts the garden city of memory with today's Bengaluru of glass towers on dried lake beds and gated communities. It argues the city's lakes, once an interconnected system of tanks and channels that caught monsoon runoff and recharged groundwater, tell the story best.

stories.title: Naredco and Credai want NCR construction curbs tied to pollution levels
stories.summary: Responding to the Commission for Air Quality Management's order restricting demolition and outdoor construction across the NCR from 5 to 20 November, Naredco and Credai asked for curbs linked to actual pollution levels. Blanket restrictions, they said, could disrupt realty projects. Essential public infrastructure is exempt.

stories.title: Heat maps help Vietnamese cities decide who to cool first
stories.summary: Research from RMIT University Vietnam shows heat maps combined with social data can help cities target cooling where it matters, by asking who lives there and how well they cope. The issue comes as Vietnam may enter a new El Nino cycle in 2026 to 2027.

stories.title: Greening could cool Fukuyama's station square by nearly 0.6 degrees
stories.summary: A study in City and Built Environment combined five days of field measurements with simulations of the square south of Fukuyama Station in Japan. Covering its bus dominated tarmac with grass and trees could cool it by nearly 0.6 degrees Celsius. The city is already planning to reorganise the space.

stories.title: Oxford Street is closed to traffic. Dezeen asks what comes next
stories.summary: The UK's busiest shopping street is now closed to vehicles, and Dezeen's weekly podcast asks about the long term plan and why bum sensing picnic benches have been installed. Nat Barker and Amy Peacock talk it through. The benches, presumably, are listening.

stories.title: A Dutch book on making room to grow with sea level rise
stories.summary: NIOZ Royal Netherlands Institute for Sea Research says a new Dutch book, Meegroeien, published on 30 October, brings together science, personal stories, essays and art on living with sea level rise. At its heart is working with the natural processes that shaped the Dutch landscape.

stories.title: On World Cities Day, a case for building cities around people
stories.summary: A Statesman column marking World Cities Day, themed Regenerating the City: Adequate Housing for All, asks whether a child can walk safely to school and whether a construction worker can afford to live near the site she builds. A house alone, it argues, is not adequate.

stories.title: Miri puts flood resilience at the centre of its urban plans
stories.summary: Miri in Sarawak is placing flood mitigation and nature based solutions at the centre of its urban development agenda. Mayor Adam Yii Siew Sang said urban flooding remains one of the city's most pressing challenges and called for integrated planning and stronger community participation.

stories.title: Niamey assesses its urban resilience to floods, drought and heat
stories.summary: Niamey, Niger's capital on the Niger River, is charting a course towards urban resilience as it faces floods, droughts, extreme heat and desertification, The Chenab Times reports. An assessment in August looked at the city's exposure to both river overflow and urban flooding.

stories.title: A Florida nonprofit plans 100 homes on land behind a community centre
stories.summary: With Miami-Dade short of about 118,000 affordable homes, Homestead nonprofit Touching Miami with Love plans a $53 million, five storey building with 100 homes for families facing rising rents. It will go on unused land behind its existing community centre.

stories.title: Scientists ask whether Himalayan slope collapses can be anticipated
stories.summary: Satellite imagery shows some Himalayan slopes move measurably before collapsing, Mongabay India reports. But the signs were not enough to predict when the slope would fail in the recent Nepal disaster. Experts are calling for better local forecasts and monitoring tied to early warning.

stories.title: Arizona researchers study how black widows handle city heat
stories.summary: Arizona State University researchers are raising Western black widows and collecting spiders from urban and desert sites around Phoenix to compare their behaviour and development. They want to know what lets the spiders thrive near human development despite the heat. Phoenix seems to suit them.

stories.title: St Louis bets on downtown ahead of the 2028 Olympics
stories.summary: St Louis is making its urban core a priority, betting on office to residential conversions, innovation zones and private sector partnerships to tackle vacancies and blight and improve public safety, Smart Cities Dive reports. Only the teaser was available to us.

stories.title: Dream raises $17 million to build AI models of the built world
stories.summary: Dream, founded by former Palantir leaders Andy Elder and Arjun Mathur, has emerged from stealth with $17 million in seed funding from investors including Andreessen Horowitz. It is building what it calls built world models, aiming for engineering grade output. It calls the capability structural cognition.

stories.title: TechnoStruct becomes an Autodesk reseller and launches Newton in Mumbai
stories.summary: At the Mumbai chapter of its Tech Talks 2026, TechnoStruct announced an authorised Autodesk reseller partnership in India and introduced Newton. Speakers discussed BIM adoption in India and the West, predictive analytics, and the difference between digital doubles and digital twins.

stories.title: A 3D printed facade controls daylight and grows plants
stories.summary: Researchers designed and built a scaled prototype facade printed in two materials at once, a translucent polymer that tunes daylight and a porous medium where plants can grow. Published in Architectural Intelligence, the study applied it to a retrofit of the UCL Institute of Archaeology in London.

stories.title: Mary Duggan and RUFFARCHITECTS win the RIBA Stirling Prize
stories.summary: Mary Duggan of Mary Duggan Architects, a University of Brighton alumna, won the 2026 RIBA Stirling Prize with RUFFARCHITECTS for Lion Green Road, a 157 home development in Coulsdon, south London. The Stirling is the UK's most prestigious architecture award.

stories.title: If AI does junior architects' work, where do they learn?
stories.summary: A Parametric Architecture essay notes that architects learn by doing work that is not yet important, drawing details, revising plans and checking dimensions. It asks what happens to that apprenticeship when AI does the junior architect's work. The mistakes used to be the curriculum.

stories.title: Zaha Hadid's work traced through 15 projects
stories.summary: Born in Baghdad on 31 October 1950, Zaha Hadid studied mathematics in Beirut, then at the Architectural Association, and opened her London office in 1979. She was long called a paper architect, since little was built, until the Vitra Fire Station was completed in 1993.

stories.title: Basque architecture biennial opens a 150,000 euro call for projects
stories.summary: Mugak, the International Architecture Biennial of the Basque Country, has launched OPEN Mugak 2027, a call for cultural projects for its sixth edition, which runs from October 2027 to February 2028. The total budget is 150,000 euros and applications are open worldwide until 25 November 2026.

stories.title: A student challenge to design adventure play for London children
stories.summary: A student design challenge invites students and recent graduates to design play opportunities for children in London using free or low cost materials, simple enough for volunteers to build. Winners in each category will see their designs built in an adventure playground.

stories.title: A Paris area school swaps asphalt for planting and a simple canopy
stories.summary: 127af transformed the asphalt schoolyard at Paul Bert Elementary School in Itteville, south of Paris, into a planted landscape with a new canopy. The 1,600 square metre project explores how simple materials and techniques can make a cooler, more inclusive environment for children.

stories.title: A new history of SCI-Arc in the 1970s and 1980s
stories.summary: With and Without Walls traces the Southern California Institute of Architecture through the 1970s and 1980s. Ray Kappe proposed the school in 1972 after leaving Cal Poly Pomona amid feelings of bureaucratic and ideological oppression, and became its first director.

stories.title: Social housing and a family home win New Zealand design awards
stories.summary: Bledisloe Social Housing in Marewa, Napier, and a home in Havelock North won national honours at the ADNZ Resene Architectural Design Awards, taking the National Award for Multi-Unit Housing and the National Award for New Homes, after regional wins earlier in the year.

stories.title: A Genoa exhibition asks what a house is, through Casa del Mutilato
stories.summary: Fondazione ANMIG Genova presents Eugenio Fuselli. What Is a House?, an exhibition of drawings, documents, sculpture, paintings and photographs about Casa del Mutilato in Genoa, one of the masterpieces of Rationalist architecture in Liguria.

stories.title: A student columnist wants Ball State to rethink its shoebox buildings
stories.summary: A Ball State Daily News columnist argues for rethinking school architecture, praising the 1935 Fine Arts Building for its stonework and five triangular roofs. Like most buildings on campus it is brick, but the writer says its geometry makes it less flat faced than the rest.

research.title: Scientists discover metals that defy the deep freeze at -424°F
research.summary: Scientists have discovered a surprising mechanism that allows certain metals to resist cracking at temperatures as low as -253°C (-424°F), when similar materials typically become dangerously brittle. Instead of breaking, two experimental alloys reorganize their internal structures, creating new ways to absorb stress and remain flexible.

research.title: Scientists smash oxygen nuclei to recreate matter from the Big Bang
research.summary: Scientists have recreated a primordial state of matter from the dawn of the universe by colliding oxygen nuclei at nearly the speed of light. The surprising results show that this exotic substance can form in smaller, lower-energy collisions than previously demonstrated, challenging the known boundaries of early-universe physics.

research.title: Scientists confirm global warming is accelerating faster than ever recorded
research.summary: Earth is warming faster than ever recorded, with scientists detecting a major acceleration in global temperatures since around 2015. A new study reveals that the warming rate has surged to approximately 0.35°C per decade, nearly double the average pace observed from 1970 to 2015. After removing natural climate.

research.title: The asteroid killed the dinosaurs. Why did crocodiles survive?
research.summary: Scientists may have solved a 66-million-year-old mystery: how crocodiles survived the asteroid that wiped out the dinosaurs. A sweeping analysis of fossils and ancient climates suggests that their preference for warm environments placed them in tropical refuges that remained habitable even after the catastrophic impact.

research.title: A train was delayed by a solar storm. But something didn't add up.
research.summary: Scientists have cracked a 178-year-old mystery surrounding a train delayed by a solar storm, revealing that the famous incident happened in 1848 rather than 1841. The discovery rewrites the early history of space weather and highlights a threat that still endangers modern power grids, satellites, and communication systems.

research.title: Hurricane warning maps are improving, but a dangerous problem remains
research.summary: A new study reveals that improved hurricane forecast graphics may help people identify threatened areas without making them more likely to recognize the danger or take protective action. Researchers also found that a widespread misunderstanding of the hurricane cone persists, highlighting a potentially dangerous gap between accurate forecasts.

research.title: Scientists reach the ultimate quantum limit on a surface
research.summary: Scientists have achieved a quantum breakthrough by creating an ultra-clean surface where individual molecules can maintain their delicate quantum properties at the fundamental limit. The discovery could unlock unprecedented control over molecules and help drive the next generation of quantum technologies.

research.title: A simple touch can bring dying corals back to life in just 7 weeks
research.summary: Scientists have discovered that severely bleached corals can make a remarkable comeback simply by touching healthy, genetically identical corals. In laboratory experiments, dying corals regained their color and fully recovered within seven weeks, with as little as five days of contact sometimes enough to start the healing process.
